body:
Let $G$ be a simple, finite, undirected graph with vertex set $\{v_1, \dots, v_n\}$. Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$ and let $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, \dots\}$ denote the set of all possible colors. Color the vertices of $G$ using the following greedy strategy: for $i = 1, \dots, n$

$$\operatorname{color}(v_i) \leftarrow \min \{j \in \mathbb{N} : \text{no neighbour of } v_i \text{ is colored } j\}$$

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
solution: Official answer key verified from GATE official examination paper.

options.text: This procedure results in a proper vertex coloring of $G$.
The number of colors used is at most $\Delta(G) + 1$.
The number of colors used is at most $\Delta(G)$.
The number of colors used is equal to the chromatic number of $G$.
